extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, journalists, and historians interested in journalists killed in the United States
extracted.subtask_description: Create or maintain a chronological Wikipedia list of journalists killed in the United States, with each entry giving date, name, employer, location, and explanatory notes and supported by citations. The page also separates related categories (e.g., media workers on 9/11) and includes media and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion scope / criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous journalists have been murdered or killed in the United States while reporting, covering a military conflict, or because of their status as a journalist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include journalists killed in the U.S. while on assignment, covering conflict, or targeted because of their journalistic activity or status. The list also contains citizen journalists, freelancers and other media workers where relevant; some entries note when victims were directly targeted for investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: List entry structure (columns)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each row/entry should provide the date of death, the victim's name, employer (or role such as 'freelance' or 'citizen journalist'), the location, and explanatory notes describing circumstances and relevant context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: This list is incomplete; you can help by adding missing items. (May 2013)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page is explicitly marked as incomplete — contributors are expected to add verified missing entries. Maintain chronological order and consistency with existing entries when expanding the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use mdy dates from August 2015 (hidden category)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates on the page follow month-day-year formatting (MDY). New entries should conform to the page's date format conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements and individual list entries are followed by inline citations and a References section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support each entry and asserted trend or claim with reliable sources (news articles, books, NGO reports). Provide inline citations and full references; unsourced additions are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish professional journalists from other media workers or related cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Other journalists and media workers killed on 9/11 (separate subsection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate subsections or notes to distinguish professional, working journalists from media workers or others who died in related events (e.g., 9/11 victims who were media workers but not working at the time). Clarify professional status where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of gallery and media (Wikimedia Commons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gallery  Wikimedia Commons has media related to Journalists killed in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant images in the gallery and link to or tag media on Wikimedia Commons; provide appropriate captions and image licensing information per Commons/Wikipedia rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: See also / related topics linking
rubrics_metrics.description: See also: Censorship in the United States; Government attacks on journalists in the United States
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link the list to related Wikipedia articles (censorship, government attacks, other thematic pages) to provide context and navigation for readers.
